newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PROLONGED DROUGHT SEEN STOKING INDONESIA INFLATION.
newsitem.headline: PROLONGED DROUGHT SEEN STOKING INDONESIA INFLATION.

text.p: Indonesia's inflation rate could exceed the projected six percent for 1997 if a drought sweeping across the archipelago is prolonged, the Bisnis Indonesia daily reported on Wednesday quoting the statistics bureau chief.

Sugito Suwito was quoted as saying that inflation could be kept at six percent if the effects of the drought could be overcome, adding that agricultural production could decline this year if remedial measures are not taken.
He did not give details, but Public Works Minister Radinal Moochtar last week said the government was planning to step up artificial rain-making efforts to help farmers.
He said more dams also would be built to store rain water until the next wet season, expected to begin after October.
Moochtar said priority would be given to key rice-growing areas of Java and South Sulawesi.
Coffee traders in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sulawesi said the area had not received rains in two months.
"The weather has been particularly bad this year because in the past we used to get rains during the dry season," one said.
The El Nino weather pattern, forming in the South Pacific, is expected to peak in December and has the potential of prolonging the dry season in Indonesia, weather experts have said.
Indonesia is among the world's leading producers of palm oil, rubber, coffee, cocoa and tea.
